title: Instanton Charge, Self-Dual Bound, and BPST Example

items.title: Hodge decomposition of two-forms in four dimensions
items.design_state: Step 1 ready; current prerequisites, placement, proof contract, and scoped checks recorded.
items.statement:
Let $V$ be a four-dimensional real vector space with an orientation and inner product $g$, and let $W$ be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space. Define the Hodge operator $*_g$ on $\Lambda^2V^*$ by $\alpha\wedge *_g\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_g\,\mathrm{vol}_g$, and extend it $W$-linearly to $\Lambda^2V^*\otimes W$. Give this tensor product the inner product induced by those on $\Lambda^2V^*$ and $W$. Then $*_g^2=I$, $*_g$ is an isometry, and its $+1$ and $-1$ eigenspaces are orthogonal. Every $\Phi\in\Lambda^2V^*\otimes W$ has the unique decomposition

$$
\Phi=\Phi^++\Phi^-,\qquad \Phi^\pm:=\frac{\Phi\pm *_g\Phi}{2},\qquad *_g\Phi^\pm=\pm\Phi^\pm.
$$

If the inner product on $V$ is rescaled to $\widehat g=\lambda^2g$ for any $\lambda>0$, then the Hodge operator on two-forms is unchanged: $*_{\widehat g}=*_g$.

references.title: David Tong, TASI Lectures on Solitons: Instantons, Monopoles, Vortices and Kinks
references.locator: Lecture 1, §1.1.1, equations (1.6)–(1.8), printed pp. 8–9: the four-dimensional self-dual and anti-self-dual decomposition used in square completion.

items.title: Smooth principal bundle from two-chart gluing data
items.design_state: Step 1 ready; current prerequisites, placement, proof contract, and scoped checks recorded.
items.statement:
Let $X$ be a Hausdorff, second-countable smooth manifold covered by open sets $U$ and $V$. Let $G$ be a finite-dimensional, Hausdorff, second-countable real Lie group, and let $\tau:U\cap V\to G$ be smooth. On the disjoint union $Q=(U\times G)_U\sqcup(V\times G)_V$, impose the equivalence relation generated, for $x\in U\cap V$ and $h\in G$, by

$$ (x,h)_V\sim (x,\tau(x)h)_U. $$

Let $P:=Q/{\sim}$ with the quotient topology, write $[x,h]_U$ and $[x,h]_V$ for its classes, and define $\pi:P\to X$ by $\pi([x,h]_U)=\pi([x,h]_V)=x$. Define the right action by $[x,h]_i\cdot k=[x,hk]_i$ for $k\in G$ and $i\in\{U,V\}$. Then $P$ is a smooth right principal $G$-bundle over $X$. Its local sections $s_U(x)=[x,e]_U$ and $s_V(x)=[x,e]_V$ satisfy $s_V(x)=s_U(x)\tau(x)$ on $U\cap V$.

items.title: Trace-normalized instanton number and self-dual sectors
items.design_state: Step 1 ready; current prerequisites, placement, proof contract, and scoped checks recorded.
items.statement:
Assume full Axiom of Choice. Let $X$ be a nonempty, connected, compact, oriented, finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth four-manifold without boundary, with a supplied Riemannian metric. Let $G\subseteq U(V,h)$ be a compact non-Abelian matrix Lie group in its specified global form, let $\pi:P\to X$ be a smooth right principal $G$-bundle in a specified bundle sector (an isomorphism class of smooth principal bundles under isomorphisms over $X$), and let $\omega$ be a supplied smooth principal connection. Let $B:\mathfrak g\times\mathfrak g\to\mathbb R$ be a positive-definite symmetric bilinear form invariant under $\operatorname{Ad}(G)$. For local sections $s_i:U_i\to P$, set $A_i=s_i^*\omega$ and $F_i=dA_i+\tfrac12[A_i\wedge A_i]$. If $F_i=\sum_a e_a F_i^a$ in a finite basis of $\mathfrak g$, define $B(F_i\wedge F_i):=\sum_{a,b}B(e_a,e_b)F_i^a\wedge F_i^b$; this expression is independent of the basis. Invariance of $B$ makes the local expressions $\beta_B|_{U_i}:=(8\pi^2)^{-1}B(F_i\wedge F_i)$ restrictions of a global four-form $\beta_B$. The **trace-normalized topological charge** is

$$
q_B(P,\omega):=\int_X\beta_B.
$$

The number $q_B(P,\omega)$ is independent of the supplied connection. For a general compact matrix group and invariant $B$, it is a real characteristic number; no integrality is asserted. In the special case $G=SU(2)$ in its defining representation on $\mathbb C^2$, with $h(v,w)=w^*v$ (linear in $v$ and conjugate-linear in $w$) and $B(X,Y)=-\operatorname{tr}_2(XY)$, the associated Hermitian bundle $E=P\times_{SU(2)}\mathbb C^2$ has

$$
q_B(P,\omega)=-\langle c_2(E),[X]\rangle\in\mathbb Z,
$$

where $c_2(E)\in H^4(X;\mathbb Z)$ is the integral second Chern class and $[X]\in H_4(X;\mathbb Z)$ is the orientation fundamental class. This sign is fixed by the library convention $c(E,\nabla)=\det(I-\Omega_\nabla/(2\pi i))$.

The Hodge operator $*_g$ on two-forms is characterized by $\alpha\wedge *_g\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_g\,d\operatorname{vol}_g$ and acts componentwise on $\mathfrak g$-valued forms. Set $F_i^+=(F_i+*_gF_i)/2$ and $F_i^-=(F_i-*_gF_i)/2$. The self-dual sector consists of connections with $F_i^-=0$, equivalently $F_i=*_gF_i$; the anti-self-dual (ASD) sector consists of connections with $F_i^+=0$, equivalently $F_i=-*_gF_i$. These conditions are independent of the local section.

items.title: Euclidean Yang–Mills self-dual action bound
items.design_state: Step 1 ready; current prerequisites, placement, proof contract, and scoped checks recorded.
items.statement:
Assume full Axiom of Choice. Let $X$ be a nonempty, connected, compact, oriented, finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth four-manifold without boundary, with Riemannian metric $g_X$. Let $G\subseteq U(V,h)$ be a compact non-Abelian matrix Lie group in its specified global form, let $P\to X$ be a smooth right principal $G$-bundle, and let $\omega$ be a supplied smooth principal connection. Let $B$ be a positive-definite, symmetric, $\operatorname{Ad}(G)$-invariant bilinear form on $\mathfrak g$. For any local section $s_i$, set $A_i=s_i^*\omega$ and $F_i=dA_i+\tfrac12[A_i\wedge A_i]$. Invariance of $B$ makes the local four-forms $\beta_B|_{U_i}=\frac{1}{8\pi^2}B(F_i\wedge F_i)$ and $\gamma_B|_{U_i}=B(F_i\wedge *_{g_X}F_i)$ restrictions of global forms. Define $q_B=\int_X\beta_B$. For a real scalar $g>0$, define the Euclidean Yang–Mills functional by

$$
S_B(P,\omega):=\frac{1}{g^2}\int_X\gamma_B,
$$

where the Hodge operator is characterized by $\alpha\wedge *_{g_X}\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_{g_X}\,d\operatorname{vol}_{g_X}$ and acts componentwise on $\mathfrak g$-valued forms. Then

$$
S_B(P,\omega)\geq \frac{8\pi^2}{g^2}\,|q_B(P,\omega)|.
$$

Equality holds exactly in these cases: if $q_B>0$, then $F_i=*_{g_X}F_i$; if $q_B<0$, then $F_i=-*_{g_X}F_i$; if $q_B=0$, then $F_i=0$. Every self-dual or anti-self-dual supplied connection satisfies the source-free Euclidean Yang–Mills equation $D_{A_i}(*_{g_X}F_i)=0$, where $D_{A_i}\eta=d\eta+[A_i\wedge\eta]$. The statement asserts neither existence nor uniqueness of a connection in any charge sector.

items.title: Explicit charge-one BPST connection on the round four-sphere
items.design_state: Owner supplier repair: full source-backed mathematical construction promoted to A-page proposition; proof preserved.
items.statement:
Assume full Axiom of Choice. Let $B^5=\{z\in\mathbb R^5:|z|\leq1\}$ and $S^4=\partial B^5=\{z\in\mathbb R^5:|z|=1\}$ have the Euclidean induced unit round metric $g_X$. Put $p_\infty=(0,0,0,0,-1)$ and $p_0=(0,0,0,0,1)$, and set $U_N=S^4\setminus\{p_\infty\}$ and $U_S=S^4\setminus\{p_0\}$. Define the north chart by

$$\kappa_N:\mathbb R^4\longrightarrow S^4\setminus\{p_\infty\},\qquad \kappa_N(x)=\left(\frac{2x}{1+|x|^2},\frac{1-|x|^2}{1+|x|^2}\right),$$

and the south chart by

$$\kappa_S:\mathbb R^4\longrightarrow S^4\setminus\{p_0\},\qquad \kappa_S(y)=\left(\frac{2y}{1+|y|^2},\frac{|y|^2-1}{1+|y|^2}\right).$$

Write $x=(x^1,x^2,x^3,x^4)$ and $y=(y^1,y^2,y^3,y^4)$ for the inverse chart coordinates, so $\kappa_N(0)=p_0$, $r^2=|x|^2=\sum_{\mu=1}^4(x^\mu)^2$, and on the overlap $y=x/r^2$. The north coordinates have $dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3\wedge dx^4>0$. The metrics in these charts are respectively $4(1+r^2)^{-2}\sum_{\mu=1}^4(dx^\mu)^2$ and $4(1+|y|^2)^{-2}\sum_{\mu=1}^4(dy^\mu)^2$.

Define $SU(2)=\{U\in M_2(\mathbb C):U^*U=I,\det U=1\}$. Write $\epsilon_{123}=1$ and let

$$ \sigma_1=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \sigma_2=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \sigma_3=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad T_a=-\frac{i}{2}\sigma_a. $$

The $T_a$ are traceless anti-Hermitian generators. Set $B(X,Y)=-\operatorname{tr}_2(XY)$. Define antisymmetric symbols by $\eta_{aij}=\epsilon_{aij}$, $\eta_{ai4}=\delta_{ai}$, $\bar\eta_{aij}=-\epsilon_{aij}$, and $\bar\eta_{ai4}=\delta_{ai}$ for spatial indices $i,j\in\{1,2,3\}$, where $\delta_{ai}$ is the Kronecker delta; extend them antisymmetrically in the last two indices. For a scale parameter $\rho>0$, define $u(x)=(x^4I-i x^j\sigma_j)/r\in SU(2)$ on $U_N\cap U_S$. Form the quotient of the two trivial right $SU(2)$-bundles by identifying $(x,h)_S\sim(x,u(x)^{-1}h)_N$ for each $x\in U_N\cap U_S$ and $h\in SU(2)$, so its local sections satisfy $s_S=s_Nu^{-1}$. Take the set of admitted bundle sectors to be the singleton containing the isomorphism class of this glued bundle, and take the representation family to be the singleton defining representation on $\mathbb C^2$. Define the local connection potentials by

$$ A_N=\frac{2\eta_{a\mu\nu}x^\nu}{r^2+\rho^2}T_a\,dx^\mu,\qquad A_S=-\frac{2\rho^2\bar\eta_{a\mu\nu}y^\nu}{1+\rho^2|y|^2}T_a\,dy^\mu. $$

On the overlap these obey $A_S=\operatorname{Ad}_u A_N+u\,d(u^{-1})$, so they define a smooth principal connection on the glued bundle. Let $F$ be its global curvature, with chart representatives $F_N$ and $F_S$. In the north chart its curvature, written $F_N=\tfrac12F^N_{\mu\nu}dx^\mu\wedge dx^\nu$, has components

$$ F^N_{\mu\nu}=-\frac{4\rho^2}{(r^2+\rho^2)^2}\eta_{a\mu\nu}T_a. $$

Let $*_{g_X}$ be the Hodge star characterized on two-forms by $\alpha\wedge *_{g_X}\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_{g_X}\,d\operatorname{vol}_X$, acting componentwise on the Lie-algebra coefficients. This curvature is self-dual, meaning $F_N=*_{g_X}F_N$. With $B$ as fixed above, define the charge by $q_B=(8\pi^2)^{-1}\int_{S^4}B(F\wedge F)$ and, for any real $g>0$, define the action by $S_B(g)=g^{-2}\int_{S^4}B(F\wedge *_{g_X}F)$. Then $q_B=1$, $S_B(g)=8\pi^2/g^2<\infty$, and the action saturates the self-dual bound. This is one explicit Belavin–Polyakov–Schwartz–Tyupkin (BPST) charge-one connection; no uniqueness or moduli classification is asserted.

items.title: An explicit round-S4 spin twist has charge one and chiral index one

references.title: Konstantin Wernli, Lecture Notes on Spin Geometry
references.locator: §§1.5.2–1.5.3, printed28–30/PDF29–31, and §§2.3.3–2.3.5, printed68–72/PDF69–73; Clifford chirality, spin representation, induced spin connection and Dirac operator. The explicit round-S4 Hodge intertwiner and index calculation are supplied locally.

references.title: Wang, Wen and Witten, A New SU(2) Anomaly
references.locator: §§2.1–2.2, PDF6–9/printed5–8; real five-dimensional Dirac structure, fixed-background center transformation and periodic product-kernel parity. Its Atiyah–Singer index value is replaced here by the local Hodge calculation.

items.statement:
Assume full AC. Let $B^5=\{z\in\mathbb R^5:|z|\leq1\}$ and $S^4=\partial B^5=\{z\in\mathbb R^5:|z|=1\}$ have the induced unit round metric and boundary orientation. Let $F^+_{SO}(S^4)$ be the principal $SO(4)$-bundle of positively oriented orthonormal frames. A spin structure is a principal right $\operatorname{Spin}(4)$-bundle $Q$ with a smooth equivariant double-cover map to $F^+_{SO}(S^4)$ over the double covering $\operatorname{Spin}(4)\to SO(4)$. Use the lift obtained from $\operatorname{Spin}(5)\to SO(5)$ by restricting to the preimage of oriented $SO(5)$-frames whose first vector is the outward unit normal; the stabilizer of that vector is $SO(4)$ and its preimage is $\operatorname{Spin}(4)$. Identify $\operatorname{Spin}(4)=Sp(1)_+\times Sp(1)_-$, where $Sp(1)$ is the unit-quaternion group identified with $SU(2)$ and $(a,b)$ acts on $\mathbb H\cong\mathbb R^4$ by $q\mapsto aqb^{-1}$. Let $\Delta^\pm$ be the two defining two-dimensional complex half-spin representations, and set $S^\pm=Q\times_{\Delta^\pm}\mathbb C^2$ and $S=S^+\oplus S^-$. The Clifford action $c$ is skew-Hermitian and satisfies $c(v)c(w)+c(w)c(v)=-2\langle v,w\rangle$; in an oriented orthonormal frame define $\Gamma=-c(e_1)c(e_2)c(e_3)c(e_4)$, which acts by $+1$ on $\Delta^+$ and $-1$ on $\Delta^-$. The connection on spinors is the lift of the Levi-Civita connection. Set $E=S^+$ with its rank-two Hermitian $SU(2)$ connection $A_+$ induced by this lift.

Here a complex Banach space is a complex normed vector space complete in its norm. For complex Banach spaces $X,Y$, a bounded complex-linear map $T:X\to Y$ is Fredholm when its range is closed and both $\ker T$ and $\operatorname{coker}T:=Y/\operatorname{ran}T$ are finite dimensional; its index is $\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb C}T:=\dim_{\mathbb C}\ker T-\dim_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{coker}T$. Here $L^2$ uses the bundle metric and Riemannian volume, and $H^1$ is the completion of smooth sections in the norm $\|u\|_{H^1}^2=\|u\|_2^2+\|\nabla u\|_2^2$, equivalent to the finite-chart Sobolev norm. These are complex Hilbert, hence Banach, spaces. A smooth first-order differential operator on this compact base is bounded from $H^1$ to $L^2$.

On smooth sections of $S\otimes E$, define the full twisted Dirac expression by $D_{A_+}=\sum_i c(e_i)\nabla_{e_i}$, where $\nabla$ is the tensor-product connection. Its positive chiral restriction has the bounded realization $D^+_{A_+}:H^1(S^4;S^+\otimes E)\to L^2(S^4;S^-\otimes E)$. This operator is Fredholm, with complex kernel dimension $1$, cokernel dimension $0$ and index $1$. In the anti-Hermitian Chern convention,

$$
\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle=\frac1{8\pi^2}\int_{S^4}\operatorname{tr}(F_{A_+}\wedge F_{A_+})=-1.
$$

Its positive trace-form instanton charge $q=-(8\pi^2)^{-1}\int\operatorname{tr}(F\wedge F)$ is $1$; its connection is the scale-one self-dual BPST connection. More precisely there are unitary bundle identifications $F:\Lambda^0_{\mathbb C}\oplus\Lambda^2_{+,\mathbb C}\to S^+\otimes S^+$ and $G:\Lambda^1_{\mathbb C}\to S^-\otimes S^+$ which are parallel, meaning that they intertwine the indicated induced connections, and under which

$$
G^{-1}D^+_{A_+}F(f,\omega)=df+\sqrt2\,d^*\omega.
$$

Here $\Lambda^2_+$ is the $+1$ Hodge-star subbundle, $d^*$ is the Riemannian formal adjoint, and all Sobolev spaces and adjoints use the specified bundle metrics. In the complete twisted spinor bundle the full Dirac operator is selfadjoint with domain $H^1$ and its square has domain $H^2$. This is a direct operator calculation for this explicit bundle, not an application of a general index formula.

items.statement:
Assume full AC. A complex Banach space is a complex normed vector space complete in its norm. For complex Banach spaces $X,Y$, a bounded complex-linear map $T:X\to Y$ is Fredholm when its range is closed and both $\ker T$ and $\operatorname{coker}T:=Y/\operatorname{ran}T$ are finite dimensional; its index is $\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb C}T:=\dim_{\mathbb C}\ker T-\dim_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{coker}T$. Here $L^2$ uses the bundle metric and Riemannian volume, and $H^1$ is the completion of smooth sections in the norm $\|u\|_{H^1}^2=\|u\|_2^2+\|\nabla u\|_2^2$, equivalent to the finite-chart Sobolev norm. These are complex Hilbert, hence Banach, spaces. A smooth first-order differential operator on this compact base is bounded from $H^1$ to $L^2$. Fredholm and index below refer to this bounded Sobolev realization; the full selfadjoint Dirac operators are separately regarded as unbounded operators on $L^2$ with domain $H^1$.

For the concrete case, set $M=S^4$ with the unit round metric and spin structure induced from the Euclidean ball, take $E=S^+$ with its positive-spin Levi-Civita connection, and use the Clifford action and full Dirac operator $D_4=D_{A_+}=\sum_i c(e_i)\nabla_{e_i}$ on the complete twisted spinor bundle specified in the round-sphere spin-twist result. Let $z=-I_2\in SU(2)$ be the central gauge automorphism. Write $S^1=\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ and $t$ for the coordinate on its universal cover. Call the circle spin structure periodic (nonbounding) when lifted spinors satisfy $\psi(t+1)=+\psi(t)$, and antiperiodic (bounding) when they satisfy $\psi(t+1)=-\psi(t)$. If the gauge bundle is glued at the ends by a scalar $\epsilon_g\in\{+1,-1\}$ on $E$ and the spin bundle has multiplier $\epsilon_s\in\{+1,-1\}$, the total spinor section satisfies $\Psi(t+1)=\epsilon_s\epsilon_g\Psi(t)$. In particular, a trivial gauge gluing with periodic spin structure gives periodic total spinors; gluing gauge fibers by $z$ with an antiperiodic spin clutch also gives periodic total spinors, while the same $z$ clutch with periodic spin clutch gives antiperiodic total spinors.

Let $Y=S^4\times S^1$ have product metric and pulled-back gauge connection. On the pulled-back complex bundle $S\otimes E$, put $c_5=i\Gamma$ and $D_5=D_4+i\Gamma\partial_t$, with domain the periodic Sobolev space $H^1(Y;S\otimes E)$, so total spinors obey $\Psi(t+1)=\Psi(t)$. There is a parallel antiunitary involution $J$ on this bundle with $J^2=1$ and $JD_5=-D_5J$; antiunitary means conjugate-linear and isometric. Thus $J$ preserves $\ker D_5$, and $iD_5$ restricts to a real skew-adjoint operator on the fixed real Hilbert space $(L^2(Y;S\otimes E))^J:=\{\Psi\in L^2(Y;S\otimes E):J\Psi=\Psi\}$. The kernel of this restriction has

$$
\dim_{\mathbb R}(\ker D_5)^J=\dim_{\mathbb C}\ker D_4=1, \qquad \operatorname{ind}_2(iD_5):=\dim_{\mathbb R}(\ker D_5)^J\bmod2=1.
$$

Independently, for the general version let $M$ be a nonempty compact closed oriented Riemannian four-manifold. Let $F^+_{SO}(M)$ be its principal $SO(4)$-bundle of positively oriented orthonormal frames, and specify a spin lift $Q\to F^+_{SO}(M)$, meaning a principal $\operatorname{Spin}(4)$-bundle with an equivariant double covering for $\operatorname{Spin}(4)\to SO(4)$. Use $\operatorname{Spin}(4)=Sp(1)_+\times Sp(1)_-$, where $Sp(1)$ is the unit-quaternion group identified with $SU(2)$ and $(a,b)$ acts on $\mathbb H\cong\mathbb R^4$ by $q\mapsto aqb^{-1}$. Let $\Delta^+$ and $\Delta^-$ be the two defining two-dimensional complex half-spin representations, labeled by the Clifford chirality operator $\Gamma=-c(e_1)c(e_2)c(e_3)c(e_4)$ so that it acts by $+1$ on $\Delta^+$ and $-1$ on $\Delta^-$. Define $S^\pm:=Q\times_{\Delta^\pm}\mathbb C^2$. The Clifford action is skew-Hermitian and satisfies $c(v)c(w)+c(w)c(v)=-2g(v,w)$. An $SU(2)$ structure on a Hermitian rank-two bundle is a specified reduction of its unitary frame bundle to $SU(2)$. Let $E\to M$ be such a smooth bundle and let $A$ be a supplied unitary connection compatible with this reduction, meaning that its local connection matrices in $SU(2)$ frames lie in $\mathfrak{su}(2)$. Let $\nabla$ be the tensor-product connection induced by the lifted Levi-Civita connection and $A$. Define the full Dirac operator and its positive chiral restriction by

$$D_A=\sum_{i=1}^4c(e_i)\nabla_{e_i}:H^1(M;S\otimes E)\longrightarrow L^2(M;S\otimes E),\qquad S:=S^+\oplus S^-; \quad D_A^+:=D_A|_{H^1(M;S^+\otimes E)}:H^1(M;S^+\otimes E)\longrightarrow L^2(M;S^-\otimes E),$$

where the displayed local expression is independent of the chosen oriented orthonormal frame. Define $\operatorname{coker}D_A^+:=L^2(M;S^-\otimes E)/\operatorname{ran}D_A^+$. Assume $D_A^+$ is Fredholm; put $n_+=\dim_{\mathbb C}\ker D_A^+$, $n_-=\dim_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{coker}D_A^+$, and $\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb C}D_A^+:=n_+-n_-$. This hypothesis assigns no index value to an arbitrary bundle.

For either fixed four-dimensional background, set $H_+=H^1(M;S^+\otimes E)$ and $H_-=L^2(M;S^-\otimes E)$, and write $\mathfrak F=\operatorname{Fred}(H_+,H_-)$ for the norm-topological space of Fredholm operators from $H_+$ to $H_-$. For a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$, define $\det_{\mathbb C}V=\bigwedge^{\dim_{\mathbb C}V}V$ and $\det_{\mathbb C}0=\mathbb C$. Use the inverse determinant-line bundle $\operatorname{Det}^{-1}\to\mathfrak F$ whose fiber at $T\in\mathfrak F$ is

$$\mathcal L_T=(\det_{\mathbb C}\ker T)^*\otimes\det_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{coker}T, \qquad \operatorname{coker}T:=H_-/\operatorname{ran}T.$$

Suppose a connection $\nabla^{\operatorname{Det}}$ on this line bundle is supplied. The central gauge automorphism $z$ fixes $A$ and induces multiplication by $-1$ on both chiral section spaces, hence on $\ker D_A^+$ and $\operatorname{coker}D_A^+$. Its induced fiber map $z_*:\mathcal L_{D_A^+}\to\mathcal L_{D_A^+}$ is the dual top-exterior-power action on $\ker D_A^+$ tensored with the top-exterior-power action on $\operatorname{coker}D_A^+$; thus it acts by $(-1)^{n_++n_-}$. The constant connection path $A_t=A$ gives the constant operator path $\gamma(t)=D_A^+$ in $\mathfrak F$, so parallel transport $\operatorname{PT}_\gamma$ for any supplied line-bundle connection is the identity. For the loop closed by the endpoint gauge identification, the automorphism $z_*^{-1}\circ\operatorname{PT}_\gamma$ is therefore $(-1)^{n_++n_-}=(-1)^{\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb C}D_A^+}$. On $M\times S^1$, the product spin and compatible $SU(2)$ structures give a parallel antiunitary involution $J$ of the same type for $D_5=D_A+i\Gamma\partial_t$ with periodic domain $H^1$. The real kernel of its restriction to the $J$-fixed space has dimension $n_++n_-$, so its parity is $\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb C}D_A^+\bmod2$. This calculation does not assign an index value to an arbitrary bundle.

In particular, for the explicit round background, the fiber $\mathcal L_{D_A^+}$ has action $-1$, since its chiral kernel dimension is $1$ and cokernel dimension is $0$. The $N$-fold tensor power has action $(-1)^N$. For the fixed product background, antiperiodic total spinor boundary conditions give no product zero mode because a zero mode must be constant in $t$. This distinguishes the tested fermion-parity mapping-torus convention from an automatic eta-holonomy formula. No general spectral-flow or Atiyah–Singer theorem is asserted.

title: Instanton Charge, Self-Dual Bound, and BPST Example — Examples

items.title: Charge-one BPST instanton on the round four-sphere
items.design_state: Step 1 ready; current prerequisites, placement, proof contract, and scoped checks recorded.
items.statement:
Assume full Axiom of Choice. Let $B^5=\{z\in\mathbb R^5:|z|\leq1\}$ and $S^4=\partial B^5=\{z\in\mathbb R^5:|z|=1\}$ have the Euclidean induced unit round metric $g_X$. Put $p_\infty=(0,0,0,0,-1)$ and $p_0=(0,0,0,0,1)$, and set $U_N=S^4\setminus\{p_\infty\}$ and $U_S=S^4\setminus\{p_0\}$. Define the north chart by

$$\kappa_N:\mathbb R^4\longrightarrow S^4\setminus\{p_\infty\},\qquad \kappa_N(x)=\left(\frac{2x}{1+|x|^2},\frac{1-|x|^2}{1+|x|^2}\right),$$

and the south chart by

$$\kappa_S:\mathbb R^4\longrightarrow S^4\setminus\{p_0\},\qquad \kappa_S(y)=\left(\frac{2y}{1+|y|^2},\frac{|y|^2-1}{1+|y|^2}\right).$$

Write $x=(x^1,x^2,x^3,x^4)$ and $y=(y^1,y^2,y^3,y^4)$ for the inverse chart coordinates, so $\kappa_N(0)=p_0$, $r^2=|x|^2=\sum_{\mu=1}^4(x^\mu)^2$, and on the overlap $y=x/r^2$. The north coordinates have $dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3\wedge dx^4>0$. The metrics in these charts are respectively $4(1+r^2)^{-2}\sum_{\mu=1}^4(dx^\mu)^2$ and $4(1+|y|^2)^{-2}\sum_{\mu=1}^4(dy^\mu)^2$.

Define $SU(2)=\{U\in M_2(\mathbb C):U^*U=I,\det U=1\}$. Write $\epsilon_{123}=1$ and let

$$ \sigma_1=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \sigma_2=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \sigma_3=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad T_a=-\frac{i}{2}\sigma_a. $$

The $T_a$ are traceless anti-Hermitian generators. Set $B(X,Y)=-\operatorname{tr}_2(XY)$. Define antisymmetric symbols by $\eta_{aij}=\epsilon_{aij}$, $\eta_{ai4}=\delta_{ai}$, $\bar\eta_{aij}=-\epsilon_{aij}$, and $\bar\eta_{ai4}=\delta_{ai}$ for spatial indices $i,j\in\{1,2,3\}$, where $\delta_{ai}$ is the Kronecker delta; extend them antisymmetrically in the last two indices. For a scale parameter $\rho>0$, define $u(x)=(x^4I-i x^j\sigma_j)/r\in SU(2)$ on $U_N\cap U_S$. Form the quotient of the two trivial right $SU(2)$-bundles by identifying $(x,h)_S\sim(x,u(x)^{-1}h)_N$ for each $x\in U_N\cap U_S$ and $h\in SU(2)$, so its local sections satisfy $s_S=s_Nu^{-1}$. Take the set of admitted bundle sectors to be the singleton containing the isomorphism class of this glued bundle, and take the representation family to be the singleton defining representation on $\mathbb C^2$. Define the local connection potentials by

$$ A_N=\frac{2\eta_{a\mu\nu}x^\nu}{r^2+\rho^2}T_a\,dx^\mu,\qquad A_S=-\frac{2\rho^2\bar\eta_{a\mu\nu}y^\nu}{1+\rho^2|y|^2}T_a\,dy^\mu. $$

On the overlap these obey $A_S=\operatorname{Ad}_u A_N+u\,d(u^{-1})$, so they define a smooth principal connection on the glued bundle. Let $F$ be its global curvature, with chart representatives $F_N$ and $F_S$. In the north chart its curvature, written $F_N=\tfrac12F^N_{\mu\nu}dx^\mu\wedge dx^\nu$, has components

$$ F^N_{\mu\nu}=-\frac{4\rho^2}{(r^2+\rho^2)^2}\eta_{a\mu\nu}T_a. $$

Let $*_{g_X}$ be the Hodge star characterized on two-forms by $\alpha\wedge *_{g_X}\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_{g_X}\,d\operatorname{vol}_X$, acting componentwise on the Lie-algebra coefficients. This curvature is self-dual, meaning $F_N=*_{g_X}F_N$. With $B$ as fixed above, define the charge by $q_B=(8\pi^2)^{-1}\int_{S^4}B(F\wedge F)$ and, for any real $g>0$, define the action by $S_B(g)=g^{-2}\int_{S^4}B(F\wedge *_{g_X}F)$. Then $q_B=1$, $S_B(g)=8\pi^2/g^2<\infty$, and the action saturates the self-dual bound. This is one explicit Belavin–Polyakov–Schwartz–Tyupkin (BPST) charge-one connection; no uniqueness or moduli classification is asserted.
